content.title: About
content.content: Chocolate pancakes are thin fried cakes made from a batter of flour, milk and eggs, with melted dark chocolate or a chocolate filling added. The dish is popular in fast‑food outlets and restaurants as a quick sweet breakfast or dessert.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Traditional pancakes originated in ancient Russia, while chocolate versions became widespread in the 20th century.
In Japan a similar dish called okonomiyaki is sometimes served with chocolate sauce, but in Russia chocolate pancakes are usually topped with butter and berries.
The Guinness World Record for the largest serving of chocolate pancakes weighs over 200 kg.
Chocolate pancakes are often served with ice cream, creating a hot‑cold contrast.
Vegetarians can make them without eggs, using substitutes such as flaxseed meal.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: Carbohydrates from flour and sugar quickly provide glucose, useful before physical activity.

items.title: Contains protein
items.content: Eggs and milk in the batter supply high‑quality protein needed for muscle repair.

items.title: Antioxidants from chocolate
items.content: Dark chocolate is rich in flavonoids that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Calcium and vitamin D
items.content: Milk adds calcium for bone health, and vitamin D improves its absorption.

items.title: Fiber when served with fruit
items.content: Adding berries or banana increases dietary fiber, supporting digestion.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Chocolate pancakes can contain a lot of sugar, which is unsuitable for people with diabetes.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Standard flour contains gluten; those with celiac disease should use gluten‑free alternatives.

items.title: Lactose
items.content: Milk in the batter may cause issues for individuals with lactose intolerance.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Chocolate pancakes are calorie‑dense; portion control is recommended to avoid overeating.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the pancakes hot, drizzled with melted chocolate, dusted with powdered sugar, and garnished with berries, fruit slices or ice cream. They can be eaten with a fork and knife or rolled up like a wrap.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep cooked pancakes in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 days. Reheat on a skillet or in the microwave before serving to restore softness.
